items.headline: [R] Are there ML approaches for prioritizing and routing “important” signals across complex systems?
items.summary: I’ve been reading more about attention mechanisms in transformers and how they effectively learn to weight and prioritize relevant inputs within a sequence. This made me wonder about a related (but slightly different) problem: prioritization and routing of signals across systems, not just within a model. items.headline: Robots won't take your job. They'll bury you in work.
items.summary: Everyone talks about AI replacing developers. Here's what actually happened to me. I had a CRM project. Started 2019, one developer, 80 commits/month. By summer 2024 - zero commits, at least a year left. Plugged in AI winter 2025. Done in 2 months. Then things got weird. items.summary:
arXiv:2603.28686v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The growing adoption of Rust for its memory safety and performance has increased the demand for effective migration of legacy C codebases. However, existing rule-based translators (e.g., \ctorust) often generate verbose, non-idiomatic code that preserves unsafe C semantics, limiting readability, maintainability, and practical adoption.
